decision: require bounded wire JSON at the split-domain evidence importer
problem: the importer enforced byte limits only for string/Buffer evidence; pre-parsed objects bypassed the wire-size authority and could move arbitrarily large evidence across the qualification boundary

correctness.reason: qualification now evaluates the exact serialized artifact emitted by each trust-domain exporter rather than an unbounded reconstructed object

robustnessSecurity.reason: prevents byte-limit bypass and keeps parsing, schema validation, freshness binding, domain binding, SHA binding, and artifact verification in one authority

latencyResources.reason: one JSON parse per export, no extra qrexec round trip, daemon, database, WAL, watcher, or persistent state

regressionRisk.reason: exporters already emit JSON strings and existing production composition consumes wire output, so the change removes an unsafe alternate representation instead of adding a new protocol

qa.reason: tests now prove both normal and oversized pre-parsed objects are rejected before artifact qualification

rejected.approach: accept objects and estimate JSON.stringify size
rejected.reason: re-serialization is not the original trust-domain wire representation and may create large transient allocations before the bound is enforced
qualification boundaries should enforce their own resource contract and must not depend on every future wrapper preserving wire form
adds lifecycle and privilege surface without improving this local parsing boundary

lessons: resource bounds are only authoritative when enforced before parsing or reconstruction
split-domain provenance should preserve the exact bounded wire artifact until the authoritative importer
security gates should remove unsafe alternate input forms rather than normalize them silently
safety: synthetic/defensive Qubes qualification only; no real financial transactions or weakened security controls
